chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:

I asked him about a man in ihram who had intercourse with his wife while she was also in ihram. He said: 'Whether they are both ignorant or both knowledgeable.' I said: 'Answer me regarding both cases.' He said: 'If they are both ignorant, they seek forgiveness from their Lord and proceed with their Hajj, and there is no penalty upon them. But if they are both knowledgeable, they are separated from the place where they committed the act, and upon them is a camel, and upon them is the Hajj of the following year. When they reach the place where they committed the act, they are separated until they complete their rituals and return to the place where they committed what they committed.' I said: 'Which of the two Hajjs is theirs?' He said: 'The first one in which they committed what they committed, and the second one is a penalty upon them.'

key_terms.اَلْحَجُّ مِنْ قَابِلٍ: The Hajj of the following year
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (a specific type of sacrificial animal penalty)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a couple who both have sexual intercourse while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the *kaffarah* for conjugal relations during Hajj, distinguishing between ignorance (*jahil*) and knowledge (*'alim*) as the determining factors for liability. The ruling mandates that if both are ignorant, they merely seek forgiveness and continue, whereas if both are knowledgeable, they must offer a camel (*badanah*), perform a second Hajj as expiation, and temporarily separate at the specific site of the act until their rituals are completed. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the mental state of the pilgrim in determining the severity of the penalty.
